title: Why is IT now involved in B2B payments decisions?
summary: See why IT is playing a bigger role in B2B payments decisions and how finance and technology teams can work together to evaluate solutions.
body_markdown:
### Share


IT is involved because payments platforms now work like software infrastructure. They connect to ERP (enterprise resource planning) systems, run through APIs (application programming interfaces), and automate workflows, so technical teams have to evaluate and maintain them. Finance still plays a leading role, and the decision is now shared.


The data reflects this. In the[WEX 2027 B2b payments trends report](https://one.wexinc.com/2027-b2b-payments-trends/?cc=701Uo00000mCVFiIAO&_gl=1*sjg7wq*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3ODk1NzEzMjIuQ2p3S0NBand6TlRVQmhBakVpd0E3emN2V3NWWndNREdxZi1SZHVPZE1XODNXQ3UtS29ValJlc2RnbUU3X09EUHlSOW9PRk9BRmRkaElCb0NnWndRQXZEX0J3RQ..*_gcl_au*NTAzNzgyMDI4LjE3OTEyMTkzNTY.*_ga*MTgyNjgxMzU1MC4xNzY1NDg0MTUy*_ga_K3HRZM070M*czE3OTM4MTk4MjQkbzEwNzckZzAkdDE3OTM4MTk4MjQkajYwJGwwJGgw) , 32% of surveyed payment decision-makers work in IT, technology, or engineering, the largest single job function in the sample. Finance and accounting came second at 25%.

### **Who is in the room when payments decisions get made?**


Finance leadership still appears most often, and IT and technology teams now appear regularly alongside it. In the same research, finance leadership was involved in 86% of organizations’ payment decisions, IT in 45%, treasury in 39%, and technology teams in 35%.


Those numbers describe a shared table. Many organizations still picture Finance, Treasury, and Procurement as the decision-makers, and the data shows technical stakeholders sitting beside them.


### **What changed to bring IT into payments?**


Payments moved from a standalone finance task into the software a business already runs. Ron Griswold, director of embedded payments at WEX, put it this way in a 2026 PYMNTS interview: payments went from being[“just a line on a P&L”](https://www.pymnts.com/news/payments-innovation/2026/wex-says-faster-payments-need-smarter-brakes/) to something that can drive product roadmaps and customer retention.


Buyer expectations follow the same pattern. In WEX’s trends research, 75% of organizations expect easy integration with their ERP or AP (accounts payable) systems, 66% expect well-documented APIs, and 60% expect support for automation workflows. Engineering teams usually own all three.


### **What do IT and finance each care about?**


The two groups often weigh different things, and many priorities overlap.


**Topic** **Finance and treasury** **IT and product teams**


Cost Cost control, rebates, working capital Total integration and maintenance effort


Risk Fraud exposure, compliance, controls Security architecture, authentication, reliability


Speed Payment timing and cash flow certainty Time to integrate and go live


Data Reconciliation and reporting API access, data formats, documentation


Scale Supplier coverage and payment mix How the system handles growth and new payment types


Fragmentation concerns both groups. In the[WEX 2026 Business Payments Report](https://one.wexinc.com/cps-2026-state-of-payments-survey/?cc=701Uo00000mCZG9IAO) , 91% of organizations use two or more platforms. The report notes that for technology teams, each additional platform can mean duplicate integrations, multiple APIs, and separate authentication frameworks.


### **Why does early IT involvement matter?**


Integration is where many payment projects slow down, and IT teams can see the problems earlier. In WEX’s 2026 research,[implementation cost (51%), integration with existing systems (41%), and change management (38%)](https://finviz.com/news/404663/wex-survey-reveals-85-of-businesses-face-internal-obstacles-to-b2b-payment-modernization) were the top barriers to adopting new payment technology.


Timelines show the stakes. Among organizations that adopted a new payment solution in the past 12 to 24 months, 40% took four to six months to integrate it, 23% took seven months or more, and 5% never completed the integration.


Eric Frankovic, head of Corporate Payments at WEX, has pointed to early architecture choices as a major factor. His advice:[“The key is to avoid one-off integrations.”](https://www.pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2026/wex-says-embedded-payments-are-easier-to-launch-than-to-scale/) He said small early decisions can become expensive later. That interview focused on embedded programs, but the logic applies to any payments project connected to core systems.


He made a related point in 2024:[“Integrating payments into complex tech environments is a struggle.”](https://www.pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2024/three-hidden-assets-that-define-modern-business-payments/) He added that a provider with the right expertise can make a difference.


### **How can finance and IT make payments decisions together?**


- Bring IT in when you define requirements, before you shortlist providers.
- Agree on shared criteria, such as ERP integration, API documentation, fraud controls, and supplier coverage.
- Ask technical and finance stakeholders to review the same demo.
- Decide up front who owns the program after launch, including support and ongoing changes.


### **FAQ**


#### **Does this mean finance is losing control of payments?**


No. Finance leadership was the most frequently cited group in WEX’s research, at 86% of organizations. The change is that IT and technology teams now appear in the same decisions, so the work is shared.


#### **How early should IT get involved in a payments project?**


Early enough to shape the requirements. In WEX’s research,[integration challenges (41%) and change management hurdles (38%)](https://finviz.com/news/404663/wex-survey-reveals-85-of-businesses-face-internal-obstacles-to-b2b-payment-modernization) ranked among the top barriers to adopting new payment technology. IT teams usually see integration risks before finance teams do.
